title: Story contract
description: The nine sentences the guide asks for before drawing shots: want, stakes, constraint, choice, escalation, knowledge (viewer, character, still uncertain), plant, reversal and consequence. Optional fields name the comedy mechanisms in play and the suspense question. A complete contract is a writing gate, not evidence that the story works.

premise_ref.description: Catalogue id (EDU001), board id or path of the draft.

want.description: What does the protagonist actively want before the film ends?

stakes.description: What visibly changes if they fail, and why should this particular character care?

constraint.description: What prevents the obvious solution? Establish it early enough to feel fair.

choice.description: What does the character do that causes the next complication?

escalation.description: How does each attempt change the situation rather than reset it?

plant.description: Which visible detail will matter later? The viewer must have a fair chance to notice it.

reversal.description: How does the final action use established information in a surprising way?

consequence.description: What final image shows that the character or situation has changed?

knowledge.description: What does the viewer know, what does the character know, and what is still uncertain?
